note: Non-bile-acid FXR agonists (cilofexor, EDP-305, tropifexor, vonafexor) reproduced rodent target engagement and short-term ALT and liver-fat falls, but rodent fibrosis reversal and cholesterol lowering did not carry into patients.
label: MASH (FXR agonists)

engagement.note: Tropifexor induced FXR target genes (Shp, Fgf15, Cyp7a1 repression) in rodent tissues; no human readout yet.
engagement.quote: Potent in vivo activity was demonstrated in rodent PD models by measuring the induction of FXR target genes in various tissues.

engagement.confidence_note: full text read (PMC7187203); registry record for the first-in-human study not found on ClinicalTrials.gov
engagement.note: Healthy volunteers on tropifexor showed dose-dependent FGF19 rises and C4 falls, the human counterpart of the rodent Fgf15/Shp signature.
engagement.short: FGF19 up, C4 down in volunteers
engagement.quote: Single and multiple doses showed dose-dependent increases in fibroblast growth factor 19.
engagement.judgement: Paired: Badman cites rodent target engagement but does not set the numbers side by side, so comparison_stated is false. FGF19 is the product of an FXR target gene, scored proximal. The same markers moved in patients: FLIGHT-FXR (FGF19 up, C4 down at week 6), cilofexor phase 2 (C4 and primary bile acids down, Patel 2020, doi:10.1002/hep.31205).

dose.confidence_note: full text read (PMC6672390); absence of an exposure comparison is a negative finding
dose.note: Mouse efficacy at 0.03-0.9 mg/kg; no published mapping of mouse exposure to human dose for any member; human doses set on FGF19 and pruritus.
dose.short: Mouse doses never mapped to humans
dose.quote: The efficacy of tropifexor at <1 mg/kg doses was superior to that of OCA at 25 mg/kg in the liver in both NASH models.
dose.judgement: FLIGHT-FXR chose 10-90 ug 'based on preclinical results, safety and pharmacological activity' and escalated to 140-200 ug on a human exposure-response analysis (AUC > 40 ng*h/mL), not on a model target. Cilofexor: rat efficacy at 10-30 mg/kg (Schwabl 2021) but ATLAS used 30 mg, the dose that barely moved liver fat in Patel 2020 (-1.8% vs +1.9%); no exposure multiple published. EDP-305 (30 mg/kg rodents vs 1-2.5 mg) and vonafexor likewise unmapped. No stated tolerability margin, so decision 16 does not apply.

efficacy.model: Rat BDL and mouse CDAHFD fibrosis (EDP-305)
efficacy.note: EDP-305 30 mg/kg reduced fibrosis in bile-duct-ligated rats and CDAHFD mice; no patient data yet.
efficacy.quote: High-dose EDP-305 (30 mg/kg) reduced liver fibrosis in both the BDL and CDAHFD models as measured by collagen proportional area, hydroxyproline analysis, and fibrogenic gene expression (all P < 0.05).

efficacy.confidence_note: abstract-level for both papers (PubMed 33169409, 33435509); contra is a judgement call
efficacy.model: Choline-deficient high-fat diet plus nitrite NASH rats (cilofexor)
efficacy.note: Cilofexor cut rat fibrosis area 41-69% and portal pressure; in ATLAS (F3-F4) cilofexor 30 mg monotherapy improved fibrosis in 12% vs 11% placebo.
efficacy.quote: The primary endpoint was achieved in 11% of placebo-treated patients versus cilofexor/firsocostat (21%; P = 0.17), cilofexor/selonsertib (19%; P = 0.26), firsocostat/selonsertib (15%; P = 0.62), firsocostat (12%; P = 0.94), and cilofexor (12%; P = 0.96).
efficacy.judgement: Year 2021 because the sponsor-coauthored rat paper (Gilead/Phenex; Schwabl 2021, epub 2021-01-09) became public after ATLAS results (registry 2020-12-03, Loomba epub 2020-11). Not marked a retrodiction: the rat work was a development study by the sponsors and nothing shows it was run after ATLAS read out; a re-scorer treating publication date as run date would make it retrodiction contra, same status. ATLAS used 30 mg, weak on liver fat in Patel 2020, so dose may share the blame; the dose cell stays untested for want of a stated target. Population F3-F4 (56% cirrhosis) matches the rat's portal-hypertensive stage.

efficacy.magnitude_basis: hepatic fat fraction and ALT change vs placebo
efficacy.confidence_note: full text read (PMC9941046); year from the registry results posting; status follows the week-12 primary endpoints
efficacy.note: Mice predicted falls in steatosis and liver injury; FLIGHT-FXR's week-12 primary endpoints moved for ALT and liver fat, not AST; 48-week fibrosis did not improve.
efficacy.short: ALT, fat fell; AST, fibrosis did not
efficacy.quote: Treatment with tropifexor resulted in numerically dose-dependent reductions in ALT and liver fat content (HFF measured by MRI-PDFF) at week 12 compared with placebo.
efficacy.reason: Primary ALT/fat matched; histology did not

patient_trials.quote: At Week 12, the least squares mean reductions from baseline in ALT for patients receiving 2.5 mg EDP-305 and 1 mg EDP-305 were -27.9 U/L (95% CI 0.03 to 24.9; p = 0.049) and -21.7 U/L (-5.8 to 18.3: p = 0.304), respectively

In Part B, there was a significant reduction in least-square mean (SE) absolute change in LFC from baseline to Week 12 for VONA-100QD (-6.3% [0.9]) and VONA-200QD (-5.4% [0.9]), vs. placebo (-2.3% [0.9], p = 0.002 and 0.012, respectively).

efficacy.judgement: Different model from the failed cilofexor rat (model_change true). The primary endpoints were week-12 ALT, AST and liver fat; ALT and fat fell, AST did not, so source_calls_it partial. The same mice also predicted fibrosis reversal ('tropifexor reversed established fibrosis'), and Part C's 48-week histology (secondary) showed no gain over placebo; recorded as outcome_tested negative because histology is the regulatory endpoint, not a clinical outcome, a judgement call. The trial paper cites 'treatment efficacy in animal models of NASH' without a side-by-side, so comparison_stated is false. EDP-305 (ARGON-1, ALT primary; rodent ALT -62% in MCD mice, An 2020) and vonafexor (LIVIFY, liver fat primary; no published vonafexor NASH model found) also matched on short-term surrogates.

safety.note: Tropifexor lowered plasma cholesterol in STAM mice; the authors doubted the model for human cholesterol effects.
safety.quote: Although cholesterol levels were down‐regulated with tropifexor, no effect was observed with OCA.

safety.confidence_note: full text read (PMC9941046); registry lipid ratios read from NCT02855164 results; quote is the clause before a semicolon
safety.note: FLIGHT-FXR: LDL rose (ratio 1.20 vs 0.97 placebo at 200 ug) and HDL fell (0.82 vs 1.03), opposite to the mouse cholesterol fall.
safety.short: LDL up in patients; mice said down
safety.quote: Tropifexor treatment was associated with an overall trend of increase in low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C) and decrease in high-density lipoprotein cholesterol (HDL-C) levels (Extended Data Fig. 2)
safety.judgement: The mice showed lower plasma cholesterol; patients showed higher LDL and lower HDL, so contra with magnitude opposite. Hernandez already flagged the STAM model as unfit for human cholesterol effects (using obeticholic acid, a non-member), which is why this is a pairing and not stated. Healthy volunteers dosed 2 weeks showed no lipid change (Badman 2020); vonafexor also raised LDL (LIVIFY). Pruritus, the class's dose-limiting harm (tropifexor 52-69%, EDP-305 50.9%, cilofexor 14%, vonafexor 18%), is not scored: no member's rodent studies measured scratching, and Hernandez's 'may reduce side effects' for GPBAR1-sparing agonists was a hypothesis, not model data.

safety.confidence_note: full text read (PMC5983391). INT-2228 and INT-2231 identified as tropifexor and cilofexor from the chemical names given in Methods.
safety.note: Tropifexor and cilofexor tool batches raised LDL-C and lowered HDL-C in mice with human hepatocyte livers; predicted a class LDL rise.
safety.short: Humanized mice: LDL up as class effect
safety.quote: Treatment with two clinically relevant nonsteroidal FXR agonists elicited similar lipoprotein and hepatic changes in chimeric mice, suggesting that the increase in circulating LDL-C is a class effect of FXR activation.
safety.judgement: Intercept-run model built to reproduce obeticholic acid's human LDL rise (a retrodiction for OCA, which is not a member); for the member drugs it was a prospective class prediction made before their patient lipid data.

safety.confidence_note: patient side full text read by the draft (PMC9941046); year from the FLIGHT-FXR registry results posting (NCT02855164)
safety.note: FLIGHT-FXR: tropifexor raised LDL-C and lowered HDL-C in NASH patients, as the humanized mice predicted.
safety.quote: Tropifexor treatment was associated with an overall trend of increase in low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C) and decrease in high-density lipoprotein cholesterol (HDL-C) levels (Extended Data Fig. 2)
safety.judgement: Paired: Sanyal does not cite the PXB study. Same direction for the drug dosed in the mice (INT-2228). Vonafexor (LIVIFY) also raised LDL in patients.

safety.magnitude_basis: LDL-C/HDL-C change with cilofexor vs predicted rise
safety.confidence_note: full text read (PMC10014688). Patel 2020 (hep.31205) reportedly found no LDL-C/HDL-C difference vs placebo in NASH patients, which would date this 2020, but the full text was paywalled and no verbatim sentence could be read.
safety.note: Cilofexor, the other drug dosed in the mice, left LDL, HDL and total cholesterol unchanged in volunteers dosed up to 300 mg.
safety.short: Cilofexor: no lipid change in humans
safety.quote: No clinically relevant changes in 12‐lead ECGs, lipids (total cholesterol, high‐density lipoprotein [HDL], low‐density lipoprotein [LDL], and triglycerides) or vital signs
safety.judgement: One drug's contra beats another's same on the same model: the mice predicted an LDL rise for INT-2231 (cilofexor) and humans showed none. Healthy volunteers, up to 14 days; the mouse dose may exceed human hepatic exposure of an intestine-biased agonist, so a dose mismatch may explain it. Quote is the opening clause of the sentence.

safety.confidence_note: year is a proxy: the screen selected cilofexor before its first-in-human studies (healthy-volunteer abstracts 2016); the model was first described in print in 2024. Abstract-level (PMID 38409114); full text 403.
safety.note: Gilead/Phenex built a high-fat-diet mouse screen on Px-102's human ALT and cholesterol rises; cilofexor was picked for minor changes.
safety.short: Mouse screen built on Px-102 harms
safety.quote: These data guided development of a high fat diet mouse model to screen FXR agonists based on ALT and cholesterol changes. Cilofexor was identified to elicit only minor changes in these parameters.
safety.judgement: Calibrated on a non-member (Px-102) human result, which is a retrodiction for Px-102 and not scored; for cilofexor it was a prospective selection.

safety.magnitude_basis: ALT and cholesterol: minor/none in mice and in phase 1 humans
safety.confidence_note: abstract-level (PMID 38409114; full text 403). Human side corroborated verbatim by Younis 2023 (PMC10014688): no clinically relevant lipid changes in volunteers.
safety.note: The sponsor paper sets the screen's minor ALT/cholesterol call for cilofexor beside its clean phase 1 safety profile.
safety.short: Cilofexor clean in mice and phase 1
safety.quote: Cilofexor demonstrated antisteatotic and antifibrotic efficacy in rodent models and antisteatotic efficacy in a monkey model, with the anticipated PD and a manageable safety profile in human phase I studies.
safety.reason: Minor ALT/lipid change held in humans
safety.judgement: Stated comparison by the sponsor, dated to its 2024 publication since the model was not public earlier. Not a retrodiction for cilofexor: the screen preceded human dosing. One volunteer had an ALT rise leading to discontinuation in Younis 2023, an isolated case; ALT was not raised in NASH patients (ALT fell, Patel 2020 abstract).
